summary: Carl Ferdinand Friedrich Lehmann-Haupt (1861–1938) worked in history and archaeology. He held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1893–1910), University of Greifswald (~1914–1915), Istanbul University (~1915–1918), and University of Innsbruck (~1918–1932), teaching Wilhelm Brandenstein.

Carl Fredrik Bergstedt (1817–1903) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He earned his mag.fil. at Uppsala University (1836–1842) under Otto Fredrik Tullberg, later studying under Christian Lassen (~1843–1844), Eugène Burnouf (~1844–1845), and Niels Ludvig Westergaard (1846–1848).

Carl Friedrich Gauss (1777–1855) studied at TU Braunschweig, University of Göttingen under Georg Christoph Lichtenberg and Christian Gottlob Heyne, and University of Helmstedt (PhD 1798–1807). From 1807 to 1855, he was full professor and director of Göttingen Observatory.

Carl Friedrich Lottner (1834–1873) was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (1851–1854) under Franz Bopp. He later served at Trinity College, Hartford, as Lecturer in 1860 and Professor of Sanskrit in 1864.

Carl Gaedicke was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Jena in 1877 under doctoral supervisor Berthold Delbrück, and also studied under Eduard Sievers and Carl Cappeller.

Carl Gustav Jung (1875–1961), working in religious studies and other fields, earned a medical degree from the University of Basel (1895–1900). He held posts at the University of Zurich (~1905–1913), ETH Zurich (1933–1942), and Basel (1944).

Carl Gustav Ruben Diehl (1906–1995) worked in religious studies and Indology. He earned multiple degrees including a Ph.D. at Lund University (1925–1956), where he served as Docent (1954–1959), before serving as Docent at Uppsala University (1960–1966).

Carl Hjalmar Borgstrøm (1909–1986) was a linguist and Indologist who earned an M.A. from the University of Oslo (1928–1936). He held posts at Trinity College Dublin, Ankara University, Lund University, and served as Professor at Oslo (1947–1976).

Carl Johan Sverdrup Marstrander (1883–1965) was a linguist who studied at the University of Oslo (1903–1907) under Sophus Bugge and Alf Torp. He held professorships at the School of Irish Learning (1909–1913) and University of Oslo (1913–1953).

Carl Maria Franz Lorinser (1821–1893) was a scholar in Indology and religious studies. He studied catholic theology at the University of Breslau (1839–1841), earned a Dr. Theol. at the University of Munich (~1840–1844), and studied at Sapienza University of Rome (1842–1844).

Carl Olson specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. Mentored by John Y. Fenton, he served as Teacher-Scholar Chair in the Humanities at Allegheny College (attested 2005–2015).

Carl Paul Caspari (1814–1892) was a scholar of religious studies and linguistics. He studied at Leipzig under Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer and at Berlin, later serving at the University of Oslo as Lektor (1847) and Professor (1857).
Carl Rabe (b. 1814) was an Indology scholar who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Breslau (~1840–1845) under the supervision of Adolf Friedrich Stenzler.

Carl Salemann (1849–1916) specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. Educated at Saint Petersburg State University, he worked there as a librarian and faculty member (~1876–1916) and served as Director of the Asiatic Museum from 1890.
Carl Schuster (1904–1969) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Sinology. He pursued his studies at Harvard University (~1920–1930) and subsequently at the University of Vienna (~1931–1934).

Carl Schütz (1805–1892) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the University of Halle, with Franz Bopp, and earned an honorary Ph.D. from the University of Jena in 1831, later teaching modern languages at Ratsgymnasium Bielefeld (1834–1858).
Carl Shigeo Yamamoto is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under the doctoral supervision of Jeffrey Hopkins and David Germano.

Carl Siegfried (1830–1903) worked in religious studies, Indology, and linguistics. Educated at Halle-Wittenberg, Bonn, and under Rudolf von Roth, he served as Professor of Sanskrit at Trinity College Dublin and later Old Testament Professor at Jena (1875–1901).
Carl Suneson (1941–1995) was an Indologist who studied at Stockholm University (1960–1966) under Siegfried Lienhard and V. Raghavan. In 1966, he became a Docent (Lecturer) at Stockholm University.

Carl Theodor Johannsen (1804–1840) was an Indologist and linguist. Educated at Kiel and Bonn (Ph.D. ~1826–1828), he lectured at Bonn and Kiel before becoming extraordinary Professor of Oriental Philology and Literature at the University of Copenhagen in 1833.
